title: How many bottles will there be after forty days?
description: A container holds five bottles and a new container arrives every day. Each day adds the same five bottles, so the total after forty days is five times forty. A short check with ten days confirms it.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the same amount is added every day, multiply that amount by the number of days. Watch for students who raise five to the power forty because the number keeps growing.

video_script.why: A fixed gain each day is linear growth, so the total is the gain times the number of days, not a power.
video_script.substitution: Find what one day adds, multiply by the number of days, then check with a smaller number of days.
video_script.anchor: five bottles in each container and one new container every day
video_script.payoff_line: A fixed gain each day is the gain times the number of days

final_answer.spoken: There would be two hundred bottles, which is two times ten to the power two.

maths_rules: each day adds one container of 5 bottles, so the count goes 5, 10, 15, 20, ...
check: 10 days give 5 × 10 = 50 bottles, and 40 days are 4 times 10 days
video_script.design: A shelf gains one container of five bottles each day. The count grows in a row of equal blocks, and the working area builds the multiplication.
